fields.meta_description: Build a law firm landing page for each practice area, with intake questions, a conflict check and every inquiry routed to the right attorney.
fields.h1: Build a Law Firm Landing Page for Every Practice Area
fields.hero_description: Describe the practice area and the cases you take. Emergent builds the law firm landing page and the intake behind it, and routes each inquiry to the right person.
fields.explore_cta: Build My Law Firm Landing Page
fields.features_heading: What Every Practice Area Page Needs
fields.features_subheading: The page a prospective client reads, and the intake that decides who calls them back and when.
fields.feature_1:
Intake questions for each practice area

Emergent writes the questions an intake call would ask first: the crash county for an injury case, the arrest date for a DUI. Each answer gets its own column in the intake table.
fields.feature_2:
Routing by case type and county

Route each inquiry by case type and county, with a backup person for vacations. The intake manager or attorney gets a Slack message or an email, and every handoff is logged.
fields.feature_3:
New inquiries in Clio Grow or your CRM

Clio Grow or any intake tool with an API receives each inquiry, tagged with its practice area and the page it came from. Nobody on the intake team retypes a lead from an email.
fields.feature_4:
Copy and fee changes by message

Ask Emergent to raise the consult fee, add a Spanish version or swap the headshot. The page updates at the same address, and inquiries saved before the change stay in the table.
fields.feature_5:
A separate page for each ad group

Request one page per practice area or per ad group, each with its own headline. All of them write to a single intake table that records the page and the keyword behind each inquiry.
fields.feature_6:
Your firm's code on your firm's domain

Export the pages, intake table, and routing rules to GitHub on paid plans. Host them on Emergent under the firm's custom domain, which uses credits, or hand them to your IT team.

fields.usecase_heading: Law Firm Landing Pages by Practice Area
fields.tab_content_1:
Injured callers with no lawyer go straight to intake

Crash victims on Marlow Injury Law's free case review page say whether they were hurt and whether a lawyer already represents them. Anyone injured with no lawyer reaches intake manager Ellen Park as a Slack direct message, with the crash county attached. Represented visitors see a polite note instead.
fields.tab_content_2:
No consult booked until the conflict check clears

Before anyone books, Bellweather Family Law's consultation page asks for the visitor's name and the spouse's full name. Both run against the firm's client list. A clean result opens the calendar. A match holds the request for the conflicts clerk, Ruth Abara, before the visitor has written a word about the marriage.
fields.tab_content_3:
Which estate plan fits, answered in five questions

Two flat fees head Juniper Estate Law's page: $950 for a will package and $2,400 for a revocable living trust. A visitor answers five questions, and the page recommends a package by the firm's own rule, such as the trust for homeowners. The lead lands in the Clio Grow lead inbox with that package attached.
fields.tab_content_4:
After-hours DUI inquiries for the attorney on call

Dorsey Defense points its Google Ads at a DUI page with a short form and the firm's phone number. Inquiries that arrive after 6 PM go straight to Nina Holt, the attorney on call, in a Slack message that includes the ad keyword behind the click. Daytime inquiries go to the intake desk.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Law Firm Landing Page
fields.howto_description: A law firm landing page speaks to one kind of case and asks for one thing, such as a case review request or a booked consult. Settle the offer and the copy first, then the intake rules that decide who calls back.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Give each practice area its own page
fields.howto_step_1_des: A visitor searching for a divorce lawyer and one searching for a DUI lawyer expect different first questions. Give each practice area a page with its own headline and one action, such as a free case review or a paid consult.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Someone who clicked an ad for truck accident lawyers should read those words at the top of the page. Google Ads can pass the matched keyword into the page URL with a ValueTrack parameter, and the form saves it with the inquiry.
fields.howto_step_3_des: ABA Model Rule 7.2(d) asks that any communication about a lawyer's services include the name and contact information of at least one lawyer or firm responsible for it. Put both in the footer, and check your state's version of the rule.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Model Rule 1.18 limits what a firm may do with information a prospective client shares, even when the firm never takes the case. Collect the visitor's name and the other party's name first, run the conflict check, then ask what happened.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask only what the callback needs
fields.howto_step_5_des: A phone number, the type of case and one qualifying answer cover most first calls. Leave the full story for the consultation, where an attorney can ask follow-up questions and explain what the firm does with the answers.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before the first ad runs, write down who owns inquiries on weeknights and weekends, and how fast a reply should go out. Put that rule in the prompt, and the page sends each late inquiry to that attorney directly.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once a month, go through the inquiries the firm turned down and note why, such as a practice area it does not handle or a county outside its reach. A reason that keeps coming back calls for a new screening question on the page.

plan.angle: The top 10 is design galleries (Dribbble, Behance, Figma, ThemeForest, OptimizePress), Unbounce's legal templates and three advice posts (Clio, Contra, Good2bSocial). The galleries stop at a hero and a form, and the posts list components. None shows what happens to an inquiry after the visitor presses submit: the conflict check, the practice-area routing, the after-hours call. This page defines the term for the AI Overview, then shows four working pages by practice area (injury case review, family law consult with a conflict check, flat-fee estate planning, DUI ad page), each with the intake behind the form, and a how-to grounded in ABA Model Rules 7.2 and 1.18 and Google Ads tracking.
tab_stories: Marlow Injury Law's free case review page asks crash victims whether they were hurt and whether they already have a lawyer, and every injured visitor with no lawyer reaches intake manager Ellen Park as a Slack direct message.

Bellweather Family Law's consultation page asks for the spouse's full name before a visitor can pick a time, and a name that matches the firm's client list holds the booking for the conflicts clerk instead of confirming it.
Juniper Estate Law's page lists flat fees for a will and a trust, recommends a package from five answers, and sends each lead into Clio Grow with the package attached.
Dorsey Defense runs a DUI page for its Google Ads, and every form filled in after 6 PM goes to the on-call attorney with the search keyword that brought the visitor.
